findings.description: Test adequacy: no test fails if the guard's `--list 'v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*'` pattern is widened or removed.
findings.body:
**Test adequacy: the guard's release-tag filter is not pinned by any case.**

The new guard only skips the run when a `vX.Y.Z` tag contains HEAD:

```bash
[ -z "$(git tag --contains HEAD --list 'v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*')" ] || exit 0
```

The mutant `[ -z "$(git tag --contains HEAD)" ] || exit 0` passes the whole suite. The only tag in the suite that is not a release is `nightly` in the case at lines 57-61, and it sits on `fix: a` with `docs: b` committed on top. It is an ancestor of HEAD, so `--contains HEAD` never lists it. Every other fixture tag is either a release tag or an ancestor of HEAD. No case puts a tag that is not a release on HEAD or on a later commit.

If the filter were dropped, a moving `nightly` or `latest` tag on the trunk tip would silently suppress every release.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/78cb96de78b7c274310996302d391b6748d18ef3/scripts/next-version.sh#L12-L12
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/78cb96de78b7c274310996302d391b6748d18ef3/tests/scripts/next-version.test.sh#L57-L61

One fix is to move the existing `nightly` case's tag onto HEAD. `describe --match` still has to skip `nightly`, so the case keeps its original coverage:

```bash
expect v1.1.1 'a non-release tag on HEAD does not suppress the release' v1.1.0 'fix: a' && {
  cd "$T/$n" && git tag nightly
  got=$(bash "$NEXT")
  [ "$got" = v1.1.1 ] || { echo "FAIL want=v1.1.1 got=$got  a non-release tag on HEAD"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
}
```

findings.description: In git's glob, `*` matches anything, including `-`, so `v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*` also matches suffixed tags like `v2.0.0-rc.1`. If such a pre-release tag sits on HEAD (for example, a maintainer tags the merge commit before the queued Release job checks out), the guard exits 0 silently. Before this change, that run reached lines 14-17 and failed loudly with "the last release tag ... is not vX.Y.Z", the behavior the suite pins with 'a v tag with a suffix stops the release'. The next push still fails loudly, so the effect is limited to that one run. To keep the error, filter the guard's output to exact `vX.Y.Z` names (for example, keep only lines matching `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`) so a suffixed tag falls through to the validation below.

Since 78cb96d, empty output from `next-version.sh` has a second cause: HEAD is already covered by a release tag on it or on a later commit (the stale re-run case). In that case the run still logs "No feat, fix, perf or breaking commit since the last release", which is wrong when the range did contain a `fix`. A wording that covers both causes would fix it, such as "Nothing to publish: no release-worthy commit since the last release, or a release already covers this commit."

The header comment says "a range of docs, chore, test or refactor commits releases nothing", but the `docs/workflow.md` row this commit changed now reads "anything else (`docs`, `chore`, `test`, `refactor`, `ci`, a revert) | no release". Wording such as "a range with no feat, fix, perf or breaking commit releases nothing" matches the table and does not need a type list that goes stale.

The header says the script prints "nothing when no commit since the last release warrants one", but the new early exit on line 12 also prints nothing when a later `vX.Y.Z` tag already contains HEAD, even if the range holds a `feat` or `fix`. Add a clause such as "or when a later release tag already contains HEAD".

The case name 'a commit no release covers yet' says the opposite of what its block tests: a commit that a later release already covers, which its own failure message calls "a stale commit under a later release". Rename it to something like 'a commit a later release already covers'.
